To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the distortion outage probability is an increasing function of the correlation between sensor node observation and source signal and that it is an increasing function (decreasing function) of the correlation between different sensor node observations when the source signal is uncorrelated (correlated) with sensor node observations.

1) the correlation between sensor node observation and the source signal, and the correlation between sensor nodes observations have significant effect on the distortion performance of the distributed estimation in WSNs; and 2) the outage probability of the distortion can be minimized by an optimal power allocation scheme that depends on the correlation between sensor-node observations and the source node.

the correlation between sensor nodes observations and the source node observations and the correlation between sensor node observation have a significant effect on the performance of distributed estimation in wireless sensor networks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of correlated observations and channel fading on the performance of LMMSE estimator.
the effect of the correlation between sensor node measurements and the source signal and between sensor node measurements on the MSE performance of the LMMSE estimator in the presence of fading.
finding an optimal power allocation scheme for minimizing the outage probability of the distortion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the correlation between sensor node observation and source signal has an important effect on the performance of LMMSE estimator in WSNs.
the inter-node correlation has the most effect on the performance of LMMSE estimator.
, the source-node correlation is the most significant factor in the performance of distributed estimation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the inter-node and source-node correlations have a significant effect on the performance of LMMSE estimator.
the correlation between the source signal and the observations has a more significant impact on the performance of distributed estimation than the correlation between the observations.
the source and inter-node correlation has a significant effect on the performance of estimation in WSNs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the outage probability of the LMMSE estimator is a monotonically decreasing function of the source-node and inter-node correlations.

, for the three correlation models considered, the source-node correlation has a significant effect on the performance of distributed estimation, whereas the effect of the inter-node correlation is negligible.

the correlation between the source signal and sensor node observations has an effect on the distortion and the outage probability, and that the inter-node correlation has no effect on the distortion but it has a significant effect on the outage probability.
